user.title: Cloudflare client certificates
user.description:
Gives every Home Assistant app install its own client certificate and revokes it when the install is removed.

Paste a Cloudflare API token. The integration checks what the token can do and picks the setup that fits:

- **Automatic:** a token with broad access (for example, all permissions on the account). The integration sets up Cloudflare for you, then restricts its own token to client certificates if it's allowed to edit itself. [Pre-filled setup token]({setup_url}): add **Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit** for the tunnel route, and **API Tokens: Edit** so it can restrict itself.
- **Manual:** a token with only **SSL and Certificates: Edit** on your zone, after you've set up Cloudflare yourself. The integration checks that setup.

This token has broad access, so the integration will set up Cloudflare for you: require client certificates on the hostname, add a WAF rule that blocks requests without a valid certificate{tunnel}. Then it will {after}.

manual.title: Manual setup
manual.description:
This token can only manage client certificates, so Cloudflare has to be set up by hand: route the hostname to Home Assistant, require client certificates on it, and add the WAF rule from the documentation. Once you enter the hostname, the integration checks that setup.

To have the integration do all this, go back and use a token with broad access instead ([pre-filled setup token]({setup_url})).

token.title: Restrict the Cloudflare token
token.description:
The Cloudflare token can do more than this integration needs ({extras}). Setup is finished, so swap it for a token that can only manage client certificates.

1. [Create the restricted token]({url}). The form is pre-filled with **SSL and Certificates: Edit** on this zone.
2. Paste it below.
3. Delete the old token in the Cloudflare dashboard.

choose.title: Restrict the Cloudflare token
choose.description: The Cloudflare token can do more than this integration needs. It can also rewrite its own permissions.

menu_options.restrict: Restrict this token to client certificates

restrict.title: Restrict the Cloudflare token
restrict.description:
The token will rewrite its own permissions to **SSL and Certificates: Edit** on {zone} and lose everything else, including the ability to change itself. The token value stays the same.

{error}

error.invalid_auth: Cloudflare rejected the token, or it can't manage client certificates for this zone.
error.still_broad: This token can still do more than needed. Limit it to SSL and Certificates: Edit on this zone.

mtls_not_enabled.title: Client certificates are not required on {host}

confirm.title: Require client certificates on {host}
confirm.description:
Cloudflare isn't asking for client certificates on {host}, so the app's certificate isn't checked and the WAF rule blocks every request. Submit to turn mTLS back on for this hostname.

{error}
